# Assumption of Moses Chapter 1 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Latin palimpsest (Codex Ambrosianus) | **Section:** Moses' Farewell Commission to Joshua

---

**1:1** The testament of Moses, which he made in the one hundred and twentieth year of his life — which is the two thousand five hundredth year from the creation of the world — in the one hundred and twentieth year from the departure from Phoenicia, when the people went out after the exodus that was accomplished by Moses from Egypt.

**1:2** According to the number of years written in the covenant, after Moses received authority from God through his prophecy and after the departure of the children of Israel — according to Moses speaking from a book, in the fortieth year in the wilderness.

**1:3** Moses called to him Joshua the son of Nun and said to him:

**1:4** Be attentive to all that I tell you now, Joshua son of Nun; for God chose me for his people in order to make the covenant with them and to be the mediator of the covenant.

**1:5** From the beginning of the world even to the end of time, Moses was prepared to be the mediator of the covenant of God.

**1:6** And the Lord spoke to me: you have been appointed from the beginning of the world to be the mediator of the covenant.

**1:7** Receive these writings that you may know how to preserve the books which I shall deliver to you.

**1:8** You shall arrange them, anoint them with oil of cedar, and deposit them in earthen vessels in the place which he made from the beginning of the creation of the world.

**1:9** For this shall be the testimony of God.

**1:10** Behold, God has appointed me to pray for their sins and to make intercession for them.

**1:11** Not because of my virtue or the strength of my arms, but because of his compassion and his forbearance he is patient and has nourished them.

**1:12** For thus says the Lord of the world: he created the world on behalf of his people but did not make known this purpose from the beginning of the world.

**1:13** That the nations might be punished and might be humiliated by the nations of his making, so his purpose might be shown.

**1:14** Yes, he devised and planned on their behalf, and he prepared and appointed me from the beginning of the world to be the mediator of his covenant.

**1:15** And now I am going to sleep with my fathers; and you will go into the land that he prepared for them.
